result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Answer A caps the reading measure at 65ch, keeps heading line-heights tight, and puts every size in custom properties that change at a mobile breakpoint, which makes it easy to paste. Its main weakness is code at 14px, which is well below the 18px desktop body size. Answer B sizes code and captions well, but it never limits the column width, its h3 line-height of 1.4 is a bit loose, and its sizes are not custom properties. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B is the stronger handoff. It caps the reading column at 65ch, keeps all heading line-heights between 1.15 and 1.3, and puts every size in a custom property that a media query swaps. A gets body, code and caption sizing right but sets no article width at all, its h3 line-height of 1.4 is slightly looser than the target, and its custom properties cover only fonts and colors, not sizes.
